- Sales: top-7 deals that may convert in next 8 weeks (Laura / Jordan)
- Infra: current spare pool, scheduled maintenance windows (Marcus)
- Finance: expected committed spend and runway implications (Ben)
- Decisions: reserve vs. burst strategy per deal + fallback mapping

Quick asks: 
1) Laura/Jordan — populate the workbook tab "Committed Likely" with estimated start week and expected sustained qps (or reserved slots).
2) Marcus — note any maintenance/driver rollout that would reduce available slots next 3 weeks.
3) Ben — give burn model with committed vs. burst cost for 50/100/200 slot scenarios.

Please reply inline with numbers. I’ll consolidate and publish a short AMR (action matrix) before tomorrow’s leadership drop.

Thanks — Jonas

Jonas — attaching a quick projection CSV (pinebridge_projection.csv) with three cost curves (committed, mixed, burst). High level:
- Committed 50 slots: $38k/month incremental (good for sustained workloads)
- Burst only (pay-as-you-go): ~2.1x per-token cost at current prices for short spikes

Relevant deals I flagged in the sheet:
- DL-47290 (Acme) — potential 12-week pilot starting wk of Mar 24, likely 40 sustained slots during pilot but only 8k tokens/day in week 1.
- DL-47620 (Pinebridge) — strong probability, needs reserved slot review for Q2 if they convert.

Recommendation: for deals that show sustained usage >6 weeks, lean committed; for trials <6 weeks, route to burst with prefix caching and KV reuse.

On cost: finance will want a worst-case committed spend per quarter. I can model 3 scenarios if you want — 50/100/200 reserves.

-Ben

Jonas / team — infra update:

Current pool status (as of 03/11 07:30 PST):
- Total reserved-capable slots: 980
- Currently committed/reserved: 745
- Free buffer: ~235 slots (includes 40 slots earmarked for burst credits)

Planned infra events:
- 03/18–03/19: driver rollout in us-west-2 (expected temporary slot reduction ~30–45 slots during 02:00–06:00 UTC windows).
- 03/22: storage node replacement (should not impact inference slots but may affect cold-start latency for cached models).

Constraints:
- If we push 40 reserved slots for Acme starting Mar 24, we can satisfy the ask, but that reduces our buffer to ~195 slots. That’s still acceptable if Pinebridge doesn’t convert in April.
- If Pinebridge moves forward earlier than expected, we need a prioritization matrix. Suggest: 1) Acme pilot (sales urgency + reference), 2) Pinebridge (higher $ but later start), 3) Orbit labs (lower immediate revenue).

Fallbacks: automatic routing to burst pool + prefix cache reuse; we can also enable temporary quantization profile to squeeze 10–15% more capacity for short windows. See runbook: On Tue, 03/11/2029 07:30, Marcus Lin wrote: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2143

I’ll update capacity heatmap and post in the shared Drive folder by EOD.

Marcus
